title: Adab with children
hook: a kiss for a grandson, a man who never kissed his own, and one short sentence about mercy

segments.voice: Yesterday: adab with neighbors, safe beside you first, then a little more water in the soup. Today, the smallest people in the house; day two hundred seventy-one let them climb on the Prophet in prayer.

A grandfather bends down and kisses a small boy. Nothing unusual, except who's watching. In Sahih al-Bukhari, in paraphrase, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, kissed his grandson al-Hasan, while a man named al-Aqra' ibn Habis sat nearby. Al-Aqra' said: I have ten children, and I have never kissed a single one of them. The Prophet looked at him, and his answer was short enough to fit on a fridge.
screen: `A KISS FOR AL-HASAN.` → `TEN CHILDREN, NEVER KISSED.` → `THE PROPHET LOOKED AT HIM.`

segments.voice: Here it is, in paraphrase from Bukhari: whoever does not show mercy is not shown mercy. In Arabic it's short: man la yarham la yurham. One verb, turned from giving mercy to receiving it. He didn't argue about customs or toughness. He tied the kiss to mercy, and mercy to the One who shows mercy. Bukhari keeps a second report like it. A desert Arab came and said, in paraphrase: you kiss children? We don't kiss them. And the Prophet answered: what can I do for you, if Allah has taken mercy from your heart? The problem isn't in the hands. It's in the heart. Then a scene you can see, also in Bukhari, in paraphrase: the Prophet prayed carrying his granddaughter Umamah. When he went down into prostration, he set her down. When he stood, he picked her up again. Nobody sent her out of the room. So adab with children isn't a list of rules for children. It's the adults' manners toward them: tenderness shown openly, affection that doesn't wait for a child to earn it, room for them even in the middle of worship. And the mercy you give a small person is tied, in this hadith, to the mercy you hope to receive.
screen: `WHOEVER SHOWS NO MERCY IS SHOWN NONE.` · `NOT IN THE HANDS. IN THE HEART.` · `UMAMAH CARRIED THROUGH PRAYER.` · `MERCY GIVEN, MERCY RECEIVED.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind a child in your life, your own, a niece or nephew, a grandchild, a student, and see their face. If one is near you today, the practice is simple: a hug or a kiss on the head, offered openly, with nothing asked back; if not, remember an adult who was gentle with you when you were small. If you pray, you can ask mercy for that child.
Adab with children. The manners of the grown-ups toward the small ones: open tenderness, room for them even in prayer, and mercy given so mercy is received. Today's word.
Your line: mercy for mercy. Given to the small ones, and given back to you. See you tomorrow.
